title: Phase 4: orders.rs dry-run then live submission
description: src/orders.rs: orderLegCollection JSON builder + dry_run:bool submission fn. Wire Submitting/PlanResult screens against dry-run only first. Then live submission starting with smallest possible real trade: decimal-quantity attempt + whole-share fallback on rejection + status polling via GET .../orders/{orderId}. Confirm fractional behavior empirically; this moves real money.

comments.author: rrajivram
comments.text:
Dry-run half complete: orders.rs (build_order_body, submit_order, submit_plan) implemented with a dry_run flag; TUI wiring via Submitting/PlanResult-style screen reachable with 's' from PlanReview, with a detail popup ('v'/Enter) to inspect the exact constructed order JSON per line - this caught a real bug live (quantity was carrying 17 significant digits of float noise, e.g. 0.26724343162931624 - fixed with round_quantity() to 6 decimals, unit tested, re-verified live).

Live-verified via tmux: built a real dry-run submission for a $1000 SIXB plan, all 26 lines correctly show 'DRY RUN — not sent', inspected the JSON body for a sample line and confirmed correct shape (orderType/session/duration/orderStrategyType/orderLegCollection with rounded quantity).

NOT done yet, deliberately: no live order has been submitted or tested. dry_run is hardcoded true at every call site; there is no TUI path that can set it to false. This needs an explicit go-ahead from the user before attempting even the smallest live trade, since accepted vs rejected fractional-quantity behavior is still unconfirmed against Schwab's real order endpoint. Leaving this issue open until that's resolved.

title: Add CLI order command for live order verification
description: orders.rs already has submit_order/OrderOutcome but every TUI call site hardcodes dry_run=true. Add a schwab order CLI subcommand (symbol, --quantity, --account-hash, --live) that reuses submit_order to let a live fractional-share order be tested outside the TUI. Defaults to dry-run unless --live passed.
close_reason: Implemented schwab order CLI command (src/main.rs, src/orders.rs::place_order_cli), reusing existing submit_order/OrderOutcome. Verified live: dry-run body correct, then submitted a real 0.5-share market BUY of F -- accepted (order 1007192550179). Fixed a stale-account-hash bug found along the way by resolving the hash live instead of trusting cached config.

title: Phase 5: transactions.rs + harvest.rs + LossReview screen
description: src/transactions.rs: fetch+parse GET .../transactions (verify date/type field names live). src/harvest.rs: pure calc (positions,transactions)->LossReviewReport, same-symbol-rebuy-within-30-days wash sale check only (documented v1 scope limitation in UI footer). Startup LossReview screen. Cross-check in rebalance.rs so a single run never both sells X at a loss and buys more X.

title: Phase 3: rebalance.rs + AmountEntry/PlanReview screens
description: src/rebalance.rs: pure, unit-tested apply_blacklist (drop+renormalize) first, then full plan-building using live prices via api::fetch_bulk_quotes -> RebalancePlan/PlanLine. AmountEntry + PlanReview TUI screens. Stop here - no order submission wiring yet. Natural demo/sign-off checkpoint.
close_reason:
Implemented src/rebalance.rs: apply_blacklist (pure, unit-tested: drop+renormalize, naturally absorbs any pre-existing weight shortfall from holdings.rs dropping cash/derivative lines) and build_plan (pure: allocates a fresh dollar amount across post-blacklist constituents by weight using live prices; tracks price_unavailable symbols separately and folds their share into cash_remainder rather than crashing). Deliberately does NOT net against existing account positions - this invests new money to match index weights, not a whole-portfolio rebalance; documented as a scoping decision. Dropped the earlier-sketched OrderSide/PlanLineStatus fields from PlanLine since they're Phase 4 (order submission) concerns with no use yet - avoided adding dead fields.

Added api::fetch_last_prices (new function, doesn't touch the existing fetch_bulk_quotes used by live streaming) since the REST quotes endpoint's lastPrice field wasn't previously extracted anywhere in this app. Falls back to closePrice if lastPrice is missing/zero.

Added AmountEntry + PlanReview TUI screens, reachable via 'p' from a loaded IndexLookup. No order submission wiring, per scope.

Live-verified end-to-end via tmux against the real Schwab API: built a real  SIXB/Materials plan (26 real symbols, real prices, correct fractional shares), verified blacklist exclusion+renormalization live (excluding LIN correctly redistributed its weight), and caught a real bug this way - Schwab's quotes endpoint hard-rejects requests over 500 symbols ('Search combination should not exceed 500') which broke a full 504-symbol S&P 500 plan. Fixed by chunking fetch_last_prices into <=500-symbol batches; re-verified the full SPY plan built correctly afterward, with BRK.B/BF.B (dot-class tickers Schwab's quote API doesn't resolve in that format) gracefully reported as price_unavailable instead of crashing. All test-created blacklist/config state cleaned up afterward. Build clean, 9 tests pass (1 network-gated test ignored by default).

title: Phase 2: accounts.rs + AccountSelect screen
description: src/accounts.rs: GET /accounts/accountNumbers (verify shape first), then GET /accounts?fields=positions (log one real raw JSON response and derive Position struct fields from it - do not guess cost-basis field names). AccountSelect TUI screen; persist selected_account_hash in Config.
close_reason:
Implemented src/accounts.rs (list_account_numbers, get_account, list_accounts) against real live Schwab Trader API calls - field names captured from actual responses, not guessed: confirmed positions[] is entirely absent (not empty array) on accounts with no holdings; confirmed currentBalances field set differs between CASH and MARGIN account types (only cashBalance/liquidationValue are common to both, used those); confirmed longOpenProfitLoss is a Schwab-computed field directly usable for Phase 5's loss detection instead of recomputing; noted 3 different 'average price' fields exist (averagePrice/averageLongPrice/taxLotAverageLongPrice) with unclear semantics - used taxLotAverageLongPrice, flagged the ambiguity in code comments for Phase 5 to resolve before relying on it.

Added AccountSelect TUI screen (Loading/Loaded/Error phases, async fetch via new accounts_tx/accounts_result channel following the established pattern) reachable via 'A'. Account numbers are masked to last 4 digits on screen. Added selected_account_hash: Option<String> to Config per plan's approved exception, confirmed old config.json (missing the new field) still deserializes fine.

Verified live end-to-end in the actual compiled TUI via tmux: launched app, pressed A, saw real 9 linked accounts with correct types/balances/position counts matching independent curl verification, selected one with j/k+Enter, confirmed the hash was persisted to config.json correctly. Also re-verified IndexLookup (SIXB) and Blacklist add/remove still work live in the same session. Build clean, no warnings.

title: Phase 1: holdings fetch/parse + IndexLookup screen
description: src/registry/holdings.rs: SSGA/xlsx parser first (covers Select Sector SPDRs incl. SIXB), then iShares/Vanguard csv parsers. On-disk cache with timestamp + stale-cache fallback, defensive header-name-based parsing. Add calamine + csv deps. Then wire IndexLookup TUI screen (read-only: type index name, see constituents+weights table). Shippable on its own.
close_reason:
Implemented registry/holdings.rs with a fully verified SSGA/SPDR xlsx parser (header located by column name not position; drops cash lines and futures/derivative overlay lines; 2 fixture tests against real downloaded XLB+SPY files plus 1 --ignored live-network test against the real ssga.com endpoint, all passing). Added TTL-based on-disk cache with stale-cache fallback. Wired a full IndexLookup TUI screen (new AppScreen enum alongside Mode, per plan: Input/Loading/Loaded/NotFound/Error phases, async fetch via mpsc channel following the existing enrich_tx pattern, TableState-based scrollable holdings table) reachable via 'i' from Watchlists.

DEVIATION FROM PLAN, tracked as follow-up: iShares and Vanguard csv parsers were NOT implemented. During Phase 0/1 research, iShares' documented CSV endpoint returned an HTML page despite CSV-looking response headers (looks like a bot-check/cache issue), and Invesco's QQQ holdings endpoint returned HTTP 406 to a plain HTTP client consistent with TLS/bot-fingerprint blocking. Writing parsers against unverified/inaccessible formats would mean guessing a schema, which the plan explicitly said not to do. fetch_live() returns a clear, honest error for these providers instead of pretending to support them. This means the QQQ (Nasdaq 100) default registry entry cannot actually be fetched right now. Filed as a separate follow-up issue.

Build clean, 5 unit tests + 1 live test all pass.

title: Phase 0: index registry entries + defaults
description: Add src/registry/entry.rs (RegistryEntry struct) and src/registry/mod.rs (load/save, lookup by name/alias). Seed baked-in defaults on first run: S&P 500 (IVV), Nasdaq 100 (QQQ), Dow 30 (DIA), all 11 Select Sector SPDRs incl. SIXB->XLB. No network yet.
close_reason: Implemented src/registry/{entry,mod}.rs: RegistryEntry/HoldingsProvider types, load/save with first-run seeding, case-insensitive name/alias lookup. Seeded defaults (SPY/QQQ/DIA + all 11 Select Sector SPDRs) verified against real curl requests: SSGA (SPDR) xlsx feeds all return 200 with correct content-type for SPY/DIA/all 11 sector SPDRs - reliable. iShares CSV endpoint returned mismatched HTML body despite CSV-looking headers, and Invesco QQQ endpoint returned HTTP 406 (bot-fingerprint block) - both flagged in code comments as Phase 1 risks, not silently assumed working. SIXB/SIXE/SIXT aliases only added where independently confirmed. 3 unit tests pass, cargo build clean.

title: Phase 0: blacklist module + management screen
description: Add src/blacklist.rs (copy watchlist.rs load/save pattern for a Vec<String> symbol blacklist) and a TUI screen off Watchlists to manage it (reuse AddSymbol/ConfirmDelete modal pattern). Validates the AppScreen extension pattern before bigger screens. See /Users/rajiv/.claude/plans/tender-wandering-lollipop.md
close_reason: Implemented src/blacklist.rs (load/save, mirrors watchlist.rs) plus a full Blacklist TUI screen (view/add/confirm-delete) reachable via 'b' from Watchlists. Builds clean.

title: Fix Nasdaq 100 (QQQ/Invesco) and iShares holdings feed access
description: Invesco's QQQ holdings download endpoint returns HTTP 406 to a plain reqwest-style GET (verified via curl with realistic browser headers - still blocked, consistent with TLS/bot-fingerprint detection, not a bad URL/query param). iShares' documented per-fund CSV ajax endpoint (e.g. https://www.ishares.com/us/products/239726/ishares-core-sp-500-etf/1467271812596.ajax?fileType=csv&fileName=IVV_holdings&dataType=fund) returns response headers claiming text/csv + attachment filename, but the actual body is an HTML page - looks like a cached bot-challenge response. Needs one of: a different HTTP client config/TLS fingerprint, a session/cookie warm-up request first, an alternate data source for Nasdaq 100 (e.g. a different tracking vehicle whose issuer's feed is reachable), or manual CSV import as a fallback path. Until fixed, registry entries with provider=Invesco or IShares will return a clear error from registry::holdings::fetch_live rather than silently failing.

title: Phase 6: fixture tests + error-message audit
description: Provider-parser fixture tests (saved sample holdings files per provider) to catch upstream format drift. Error-message audit across registry/accounts/orders/transactions modules to match stream.rs's detailed bail! precedent (401 handling) instead of bare 'request failed'.

value: Schwab's account hash (hashValue from /accounts/accountNumbers) is not a stable long-term ID -- a hash cached in config from an earlier session was rejected with 'Invalid account number' by the orders endpoint on a later run, even though it matched the same account when fetched. Always re-fetch the hash live via list_account_numbers() immediately before using it for order submission; don't rely on Config::selected_account_hash for that. Confirmed live: fractional-share market BUY orders (0.5 shares) are accepted by Schwab's orders endpoint on this account.
